prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of GLP-1 and of its biologically active form and actions, which established the basis for incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep my configuration: a single-part prize on B010 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The unanimity of the opening ballots is not my argument, and the chair is right to ask whether it reflects independent judgement or anchoring. My reasoning stands on its own. Holst established the physiology of GLP-1 secretion and its insulinotropic action, Mojsov identified the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor pharmacology and the rationale for a therapeutic strategy. Together these define the target on which every later agonist depends. The clinical consequence is confirmed by several independent randomized programmes in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, so maturity is not in question. As a clinician in autoimmunity I see few discoveries that have changed treatment strategy across so many diseases. I also think a single, coherent part is better than a second part added for balance, because none of the candidates I could pair with it has a settled attribution.
statement.case_against: The attribution is still the weak point, and I do not want to understate it. Knudsen's acylation chemistry produced liraglutide and semaglutide, the agents patients receive, and a three-name cap leaves her out. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide, set against Habener and others who are not on the credited list, cannot be verified from the supplied evidence, and I will not claim more than the record shows. The citation therefore has to be worded strictly around discovery and mechanism, so that it does not imply the laureates developed the drugs. The central mechanisms of weight loss and the long-term safety profile are also still being worked out. If the committee found Mojsov's claim unsupportable, I would not simply move Knudsen into the third place without reconsidering the citation, because that changes the prize from discovery to development.

responses.point: The chair moved from his opening trio with Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, calling the discovery claims cleaner than the translational one under a three-person cap, and listed the omission of Knudsen as the main reservation.
responses.response: I welcome that move, since it is the configuration I argued for in round 1 and I asked for your reasons. I accept your point that Knudsen is the credited name closest to the drugs, and I do not think her contribution is minor. My view is that a prize for the discovery and mechanism can be defended with three names, whereas a mixed trio invites the objection that Habener's earlier work is ignored while industrial development is rewarded. On your question about anchoring, I think the shared first place reflects the same reading of the chain. I would still want to test the Mojsov claim against the primary record, and I would not drop a two-person fallback without first examining it.

responses.point: Sandberg would accept a Drucker and Holst prize if Mojsov's priority cannot be supported, and suggested B031 or B004 as a possible second part with clean attribution.
responses.response: The two-person fallback is a real option and I would take it before adding Knudsen, since it avoids a priority claim I cannot verify. I would resist it as a first choice, though. Holst and Drucker alone leave out the identification of the active peptide form that defines the target, and Mojsov's contribution is documented in the supplied credits even if her priority over Habener is disputed. On B031 and B004 as a second part, I agree both have clean attributions, but I do not think a clean attribution is enough. The medical consequence of the unfolded protein response is still prospective, and B004 would need to be weighed against B010 as a separate achievement. I see no reason to add a part simply to use the second slot.

responses.point: Perlmann supports B005 as the strongest oncology-biology alternative and would frame the B010 citation around the hormone and its physiological actions, naming Knudsen as the natural alternative for the third slot.
responses.response: I agree on the citation: wording around the hormone and its physiological actions is the way to keep discovery from being read as development. I also agree that Knudsen is the natural alternative if Mojsov fails, and that is the same question as the chair's. On B005, I still think the mammalian survival function of BCL-2 is distinct from the 2002 work on programmed cell death, and the path to venetoclax is a real medical consequence. But the third name cannot yet be settled among Vaux, Strasser, Adams and Cory, and Tsujimoto, Korsmeyer and Cleary are outside the list. That is why I keep it as an alternative rather than a second part.

responses.point: El-Manira ranked B052 second and pointed out that the credited omissions limit fairness, and that whichever of Mojsov or Knudsen is omitted has a decisive claim.
responses.response: I agree with your point that the omission is decisive on either side, and that is why I think the citation matters more than the third name. On B052, the chair's question is whether the committee can defend omitting Eshhar while including Rosenberg. I do not think it can in the present form, because Rosenberg's work is adoptive cell transfer and not CAR design. A pair of June and Sadelain would be cleaner, but I cannot establish from the record that this leaves out no decisive claimant. So B052 stays my first alternative, not a second part. The durability and late-toxicity concerns that the chair has raised seem to me secondary, since the clinical evidence in haematological malignancy is mature.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranked B048 as the second candidate and asked whether the committee is comfortable with a discovery-only trio when clinical benefit depends on industrial analogue design.
responses.response: I am comfortable with it, provided the citation is strictly about discovery. The prize has often recognised the discovery that makes a therapy possible without crediting everyone who built the product. On B048, your attribution proposal has improved my understanding, but I still cannot find a three-person allocation among six credited names that avoids omitting a strong claimant, and the clinical impact is early. So I would not pair it with B010 this year.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide against Habener's early work can be established, which I cannot settle from the supplied evidence.
If Mojsov's claim fails, whether the right response is a Drucker and Holst pair or a trio with Knudsen, which turns on whether the citation is for discovery or development.
Whether a June and Sadelain configuration for B052 omits a decisive early CAR designer such as Eshhar.
Whether the third BCL-2 name can be settled among Vaux, Strasser, Adams and Cory without leaving out a decisive claimant.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate, and I request no recusal. My field is autoimmunity, and CAR-T (B052) is relevant to autoimmune disease, but I have no documented tie to its credited names or to those of B010 or B005. I do not infer any tie from shared institutions or topics. This is unchanged from round 1.
